domain_notes: Executed ARM instructions, not RP2040 cycles; the accepted Machine harness models ROM CLZ/memory intrinsics.
Integer speed comparisons use common finite ranges: nonnegative fractional values or signed integral values. Qfplib rounds negative fractions toward -infinity; EABI truncates toward zero.
Thumb-1 adapters for boolean comparisons and atan(x)=atan2(x,1) execute in the reference ELF; their overhead is included.
Atan outside the documented Qfplib trig range ±1024 is diagnostic only.
Qfplib has no direct asin, acos, log10 or pow equivalents. Resident float arithmetic is absent; float/double conversions remain.
qfplib.trig_domain: README.md: double-precision trigonometric functions require -1024 <= x <= 1024. Wider streams are diagnostics only and excluded from the speed gate.

implementation.conversions: Thumb-1 leaf routines normalize signed/unsigned 64-bit magnitudes, round nearest-even, and reuse the exact 32-bit normalizer for small magnitudes. Normal float/double conversion uses 13/21 instructions; IEEE special values retain the existing complete slow paths. Signed double-to-integer paths truncate toward zero and preserve the original out-of-range behavior.
implementation.comparisons: Thumb-1 IEEE comparisons handle NaNs, infinities and opposite zero signs. Ordered comparisons reverse negative magnitude order and reject NaNs before testing signs.
implementation.ln: Normalize to [1,2), use 256 certified Q63 reciprocals and Q62 logarithms, reconstruct a small log1p correction, and combine exponent*ln(2) in 96 bits. Around one, a separate 256-row Q62-reciprocal/Q70-log table retains relative accuracy; a normalized short series handles |x-1| < 2^-14. Subnormal and exceptional inputs keep the shared original path.
implementation.atan: Keep existing table reduction and inversion, replace the relative small-argument polynomial with a guarded Q62 kernel and short coefficient products.
implementation.small_trig: Normalize the remainder once, use shortened relative sin/cos polynomials and a direct tan polynomial. A second Q95 interval certificate proves 63-bit relative rounding for small remainders; uncertain cases still recompute the Q191 product. Avoid primary/tail packing and a second normalization on the certified path.
implementation.license: Independently derived project-owned code and rationally generated constants. Qfplib code/data are not incorporated in firmware.

log_tables.proof: Exact Fraction positive atanh series, 100 terms with geometric tail; both bounds lie strictly inside one nearest-integer cell. Reciprocals use exact rational nearest-even division. Both tables in the linked production ELF match every generated word; the inline log(2) constant matches the certified source.

performance.limits: Every comparable stream mean passes. This is not a claim that every IEEE input or every hardware timing beats Qfplib. The harness models ROM CLZ/memory intrinsics, and executed instruction counts are not RP2040 cycles.

qualification.transcendental_oracles: Independent Decimal 110-digit ln/log10, half-angle/Taylor atan with Machin pi; trig uses 100/400-digit reduction and Taylor sin/cos with 430-digit Machin pi. Directed tables, thresholds, signed zeros, infinities, subnormals and NaNs are included.
qualification.contract: Exact conversions/comparisons, <=1 ULP for ln/atan on this independent corpus, <=2 ULP for dependent log10; existing trig 4-ULP contract preserved with observed maxima 1/1/2. This qualification is not exhaustive correct-rounding proof.
